Visiting sick Sa'd before Badr, the Prophet preached to a mixed gathering, was rebuffed by Abdullah bin Ubai and excused him, as Muslims then forgave pagans and Scripture people.
Asked whether he had helped his protector Abu Talib, the Prophet said yes: he is in a shallow place of Fire, and would otherwise be in its lowest depth.
On a journey the Prophet told Anjasha, whose chanting drove the camels fast, to drive slowly and not break the glass vessels, meaning the women.
When fear spread in Medina, the Prophet rode Abu Talha's horse and said they saw nothing, but found the horse like a sea.
Asked about fore-tellers, the Prophet said they are nothing: a true word is one stolen and poured into the fore-teller's ear, to which he adds a hundred lies.
After a pause in revelation, the Prophet heard a voice and saw the angel of the cave of Hira sitting on a chair between sky and earth.
At night in Maimuna's house the Prophet rose, looked at the sky and recited that the creation of heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day hold signs.
In a Medina garden the Prophet had Abu Musa open the gate with glad tidings of Paradise for Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, the last along with a coming calamity.
Scraping the ground with a stick, the Prophet said everyone's place in Paradise or the Fire is assigned, yet told them to act, as each is eased toward his place.
Waking at night, the Prophet exclaimed at treasures and afflictions sent down, asked who would wake his wives, and warned the well-dressed may be naked hereafter; Umar said Allahu Akbar.
Walking Safiya home from his I'tikaf, the Prophet told two Ansari men who she was, as Satan runs in man like blood and might put evil thoughts in their hearts.
The Prophet forbade flicking stones with the fingers, which neither hunts game nor hurts an enemy but gouges out an eye or breaks a tooth.
A sneezer who praises Allah is answered 'May Allah have mercy on you' and replies with a prayer; yawning is from Satan and should be stopped; Al-Bara lists seven duties.
Allah created Adam in His picture, sixty cubits tall, and had him greet the angels, whose reply became his offspring's greeting; all entering Paradise will have Adam's form.
The Prophet turned Al-Fadl's face from a Khath'am woman asking about Hajj for her father, and told those sitting on roads to lower their gaze, harm none and return greetings.
Allah is As-Salam; the young, the rider, the walker and the smaller group greet first; spread the greeting to known and unknown, and the better of two estranged greets first.
Guests lingering after the Prophet's wedding meal for Zainab bint Jahsh brought the verse of Al-Hijab and a screen; Umar's urging over Sauda preceded the verse veiling the Prophet's wives.
A man peeped into the Prophet's room, and the Prophet said he would have pierced his eye, for asking permission to enter was ordained because of looking.
Allah has written each son of Adam's share of adultery: the eyes' is looking, the tongue's is talk, the self desires, and the private parts confirm or deny it.
The Prophet greeted and repeated words three times; whoever asks permission thrice unanswered should leave, as Abu Musa proved to Umar, and the people of Suffa asked before entering.
Anas greeted boys as the Prophet did, the companions greeted an old woman who fed them after the Friday prayer, and Gabriel sent his greeting to Aisha.
When Jabir knocked and answered 'I' to the Prophet's 'Who is that?', the Prophet repeated 'I, I?' as if he disliked it.
A man who prayed improperly greeted the Prophet, who returned his greeting and sent him back to pray, then taught him to recite, bow, prostrate and sit with calmness.

Aisha returned Gabriel's greeting; the Prophet greeted a mixed gathering including Abdullah bin Ubai; Ka'b doubted his greeting was returned during the boycott; Jews' greetings are answered 'And on you'.
Hatib's letter to Mecca's pagans was seized and the Prophet accepted his excuse; the letter to Heraclius wished peace on whoever follows guidance; an Israelite sent money with a letter.
The Prophet told the people to stand for Sa'd, whose verdict on Qurayzah, that their warriors be killed and their women and children taken captive, he called Allah's judgement.
The companions shook hands, the Prophet was seen holding Umar's hand, and Ibn Mas'ud learned the tashahhud with his hand between the Prophet's hands.
During the Prophet's fatal illness Al-Abbas, foreseeing his death, urged Ali to ask him who would rule after him, but Ali refused to ask.
Allah's right is to be worshipped alone, and His slaves' right is not to be punished; Gabriel said whoever dies without associating others enters Paradise, even after adultery and theft.
No one should make another get up from his seat in order to sit there; people should make room instead.
Guests stayed talking after the Prophet's wedding meal for Zainab bint Jahsh; when they left he dropped a curtain before Anas, and the verse against entering his houses unbidden came.
Ibn Umar saw the Prophet sitting in the courtyard of the Ka'bah in the ihtiba posture, his hand round his legs.
The biggest of the great sins are associating others with Allah and undutifulness to parents, and the Prophet sat up from reclining to warn repeatedly against false statement.
The Prophet once hurried home after the Asr prayer, and he prayed in the middle of his bed while Aisha lay before him and slipped quietly away.
Sitting on the floor beside a cushion, the Prophet raised Abdullah bin Amr's fasting from three to eleven days a month, saying none is better than David's alternate-day fast.
Abu Ad-Darda' asked Alqama of Kufa about its distinguished companions and how Ibn Mas'ud recited Sura 92, upholding 'and by male and female' as heard from the Prophet.
The companions took their midday nap and their meals after the Friday prayer.
Finding Ali asleep and dusty in the mosque after a quarrel with Fatima, the Prophet wiped him and called him Abu Turab, the name Ali loved most.
Um Sulaim spread a leather sheet for the Prophet's midday nap and mixed his sweat and hair into perfume, some of which Anas had added to his embalming perfume.
Napping at Um Haram's, the Prophet woke smiling, shown followers sailing the sea to fight in Allah's Cause like kings on thrones, and said she would be among the first.
